newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Motor delays pay after strikes.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Motor delays pay after strikes.

text.p: Hyundai Motor Co, South Korea's largest car maker, is delaying salary payments to 20,000 office staff because it is short of cash after strikes, a company official said on Tuesday.
It is the first time the company has failed to pay workers on time since the oil shock in 1979, Shin Dong-woo said.
Production lines were halted during almost four weeks of strikes called in protest at a controversial labour law rammed through parliament on December 26.
The company estimates production losses at its main factory in Ulsan at 670 billion won ($784 million).
"The strikes dragged on for longer than expected and during that time the company was not able to raise money from sales, so it is short of working capital," Shin said.
Hyundai was having trouble securing bank loans because of tight liquidity in the banking system following the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co under a mountain of debt worth almost $6 billion, Shin said.
Blue-collar workers would not be affected by the salary delay, Shin said. Office workers had been told they will be paid in full before the start of the lunar New Year holiday on Febuary 7.
On Saturday production line workers worked a full day instead of a usual half-day, and they also worked through the Sunday holiday to try to make up losses, Shin said.
